turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Saoirse, you're grand to go in. Pressure is 118 over 72, pulse 88, oxygen sitting at 98 percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): About time. I'm wrecked, and that waiting room was roasting.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): What's brought you.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm tired all the time. And I've gone mad for ice, crunching it all day.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's been this tired for weeks, doctor, I keep—
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Aoife. I can talk, yeah?
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. A couple of months? Since after Christmas maybe. I don't actually know.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Breathless.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): On the stairs, yeah. On the flat I'm grand. Stairs in the shop and I'm gasping.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She stops halfway, I've watched her.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No cough.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Weight up or down.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know. Maybe a bit down? Or not. The jeans are the same, I think. I haven't been on a scales, so.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Periods heavy.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, they're normal. Five days, not heavy, same as always.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medicines.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, what? I was miles away...
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. Right. I did take the iron, ferous sulphate, 200 milligrams. Made me sick so I stopped after two days. Nothing else.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She still has the box in the press, doctor.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. Family illnesses, quickly.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Dad had diabetes in his fifties, Mam did not, my other sister has the pressure but no sugar, and Uncle Tom on Dad's side had a heart attack around sixty. He's grand now.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Work. Drink. Food. Exercise.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Bookshop on Thomas Street, four days, about 32 hours, and I'm strict vegetarian since I was sixteen, no meat no fish. I don't really exercise at all. Glass of wine at the weekend, sometimes two, that's it.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Look up. Conjunctivae are pale. Chest is clear. Heart's regular, no murmur.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that serious or what.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Looking like low iron. I won't call it till the bloods are back.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Brilliant. More waiting.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Full blood count, ferritin and a B12 today. More pulses and greens, and leave the tea off at mealtimes, it blocks the iron.
[SEG0033] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I said that about the tea—
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I heard him, Aoife.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Reception'll book you back next Thursday for the results.
[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): I'll take her round for the bloods if you're finished.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Go on.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I have to fast? I'm starving.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): No fast. Off you go.

spec.situation: Tired young woman, strict vegetarian, breathless on stairs, craving ice; periods normal by her account; blood tests planned; diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: No nausea symptom reported; 'made me sick' refers to iron side effect.

omissions.text: Recorded symptom 'Nausea' is incorrect: the patient said ferrous sulphate 200 mg 'made me sick' and she stopped after two days, indicating an adverse effect/intolerance to iron rather than a current or resolved presenting symptom.
Breathlessness was specifically limited to exertion on stairs; the patient said she was 'grand' on the flat.
Menstrual history detail missing: periods are normal, last five days, not heavy, same as always.
